question.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{11}{12},$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}1-{x}^{2}, & 0<x<1, \\ \frac{1}{6}, & 1\le x<3, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot (1-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{6}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}-{x}^{4})\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{5})|}_{0}^{1}+{\frac{{x}^{3}}{18}|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{71}{45}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{71}{45}-{(\frac{11}{12})}^{2} \\  & ≈0.74\end{aligned}
$$

 
rounded to $2$ decimal places.
